newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beet crop heads for partial recovery.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beet crop heads for partial recovery.

text.p: Recent rains over France's main sugar beet growing area have sharply improved crop prospects after a weak start, crop analysts said on Tuesday.
But weather in the autumn will be crucial to help consolidate a partial recovery, they said.

Results of the third beet tests conducted on August 26 by sugar manufacturers and planters and due to be released later this week should show a significant improvement over the previous tests, they predicted.
"Favourable weather conditions over the last two weeks should allow the crop to make a partial recovery," one analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) told Reuters.
Good moisture levels since mid-August should boost sugar weight but cut sugar content, he said.
Results of the first two beet tests since the start of testing on July 29 have shown a sharp fall in sugar weight per hectare but a sharp rise in sugar content fom 1995's levels.
Analysts blamed the weak performance on a prolonged dry spell during the growing period.
The second test carried on August 12 showed sugar weight per hectare fell by 10.2 percent to 6.210 tonnes from 6.916 tonnes in last year's second test.
Dry and warm weather boosted sugar content to 17.48 percent from 16.33 percent.

French sugar intervention board FIRS has said it would wait for the results of the third test before eventually adjusting its June estimate of a 1996/97 beet sugar yield of 9.40 tonnes per hectare against 9.87 tonnes in 1995/96.
FIRS has predicted the sugar crop would drop to 3.9 million tonnes from 4.2 tonnes, assuming a decline in area of 9,000 hectares to 420,000 hectares.
